Here is a thorough analysis of the codebase: --- ## 1. Full Project Directory Tree ``` /vercel/sandbox/ ├── .gitignore ├── .git/ (git repository) ├── app/ │ ├── Dashboard.tsx │ ├── layout.tsx │ └── page.tsx ├── next.config.ts ├── node_modules/ (dependencies) ├── opencode.json ├── package-lock.json ├── package.json └── tsconfig.json ``` This is a very small project with only **3 application source files**. There are no `api/`, `hooks/`, `lib/`, `utils/`, `types/`, or `components/` directories. --- ## 2. Framework & Project Structure - **Framework:** Next.js (canary version `^16.2.1-canary.45`) with React 19.1.0 - **Language:** TypeScript (strict mode enabled, ES2017 target, `react-jsx` transform) - **Module system:** ESM (`"type": "module"` in package.json) - **Path alias:** `@/*` maps to the project root (e.g., `@/app/Dashboard`) - **React Server Components (RSC):** Both `page.tsx` and `Dashboard.tsx` use `async` server components --- ## 3. package.json (Full Contents) ```json { "private": true, "type": "module", "scripts": { "dev": "next dev", "build": "next build", "start": "next start" }, "dependencies": { "@ai-sdk/react": "2.0.0-beta.28", "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.17.0", "ai": "5.0.59", "next": "^16.2.1-canary.45", "react": "19.1.0", "react-dom": "19.1.0", "zod": "^4.0.10" }, "devDependencies": { "@types/node": "^20", "@types/react": "^19", "@types/react-dom": "^19", "@vitejs/plugin-react": "^4.4.1", "typescript": "^5", "vite-tsconfig-paths": "^5.1.4", "vitest": "^3.1.3" } } ``` **Key observations about dependencies:** - **No data-fetching library** (no `swr`, `@tanstack/react-query`, `axios`, etc.) -- raw `fetch()` is used - **Vercel AI SDK** (`ai`, `@ai-sdk/react`) is present, suggesting AI/LLM features may be planned - **MCP SDK** (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`) is present, suggesting Model Context Protocol integration - **Zod v4** is available for schema validation - **Vitest** + Vite plugin are configured for testing (though no test files exist yet) --- ## 4. Existing Data Fetching Pattern (page.tsx - Full Contents) This is the **only** existing data-fetching example in the codebase: ```tsx // /vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx import Dashboard from './Dashboard' // Good example: parallel data fetching async function getParallelData() { try { const [users, posts, stats] = await Promise.all([ fetch('https://api.example.com/users').then((r) => r.json()), fetch('https://api.example.com/posts').then((r) => r.json()), fetch('https://api.example.com/stats').then((r) => r.json()), ]) return { users, posts, stats } } catch { // Return mock data for build time return { users: [{ id: 1, name: 'User 1' }], posts: [{ id: 1, title: 'Post 1' }], stats: { views: 1000 }, } } } export default async function Page() { const { users, posts, stats } = await getParallelData() return (

Dashboard

Users: {users.length}

Posts: {posts.length}

Total views: {stats.views}

) } ``` **Pattern summary:** - **Server Component pattern** -- components are `async` functions that `await` data directly - **Parallel fetching** -- uses `Promise.all()` to fetch multiple endpoints concurrently - **Raw `fetch()`** -- no data-fetching library, just native `fetch` with `.then(r => r.json())` - **Error handling** -- try/catch that falls back to hardcoded mock data (for build-time safety) - **No loading states** -- since these are RSCs, the server handles Suspense boundaries (none configured yet) - **No type annotations** on the fetch responses -- data is implicitly `any` - **Inline data-fetching function** -- defined in the same file as the component, not extracted to a utility --- ## 5. Existing Dashboard Component (Full Contents) ```tsx // /vercel/sandbox/app/Dashboard.tsx export default async function Dashboard() { // TODO: This component needs to fetch data from multiple APIs: // - /api/analytics // - /api/notifications // - /api/settings // Follow the existing patterns in this codebase for data fetching return (

Dashboard Content

Dashboard data will go here

) } ``` **Key points:** - It is declared as an `async` server component (following the same pattern as `page.tsx`) - It has a TODO to fetch from three APIs: `/api/analytics`, `/api/notifications`, `/api/settings` - Currently renders only placeholder text - No API routes for those endpoints exist yet (no `app/api/` directory) --- ## 6. Layout Component (Full Contents) ```tsx // /vercel/sandbox/app/layout.tsx import type { Metadata } from 'next' export const metadata: Metadata = { title: 'Create Next App', description: 'Generated by create next app', } export default function RootLayout({ children, }: Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>) { return ( {children} ) } ``` Minimal root layout with no Suspense boundaries, providers, or global styles. --- ## 7. TypeScript Conventions From `tsconfig.json`: - **Strict mode** enabled (`"strict": true`) - **Module resolution:** bundler mode (`"moduleResolution": "bundler"`) - **JSX:** `react-jsx` (React 19 automatic JSX transform) - **Path alias:** `@/*` -> root directory - **No `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`** or other extra strict flags From the source code: - Components use **default exports** (`export default`) - Server components use **async function** declarations - Props use **inline TypeScript types** (e.g., `Readonly<{ children: React.ReactNode }>`) - No interfaces or type aliases have been defined yet --- ## 8. What Does NOT Exist | Category | Status | |---|---| | `app/api/` directory (API routes) | **Does not exist** | | `hooks/` directory (custom hooks) | **Does not exist** | | `lib/` or `utils/` directory (utility functions) | **Does not exist** | | `types/` directory (type definitions) | **Does not exist** | | `components/` directory (shared components) | **Does not exist** | | Any type interfaces for API responses | **Does not exist** | | Any `.css` or styling files | **Does not exist** | | Any test files | **Does not exist** | | `AGENTS.md` | **Does not exist** | | `README.md` | **Does not exist** | | Loading/error UI components | **Does not exist** | --- ## Summary This is a minimal Next.js 16 canary project using React 19 with React Server Components. The established data-fetching pattern is: 1. **Async server components** that `await` data directly (no client-side hooks) 2. **`Promise.all()`** for parallel fetching of multiple endpoints 3. **Raw `fetch()`** with `.then(r => r.json())` -- no external HTTP or data-fetching libraries 4. **Try/catch with mock fallback** for build-time resilience 5. **No TypeScript types** on API responses yet The `Dashboard.tsx` component is a stub that needs to fetch from `/api/analytics`, `/api/notifications`, and `/api/settings` following this same pattern, but none of those API routes exist yet. session_id: ses_2683966d7ffexooeKz7MfdZZq0
